A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LexGen research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original dictionary-generation experiments, routing ablations, Sanskrit-augmentation experiments and human evaluations in Section 5 and Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and human-evaluation results, plus vocabulary-overlap, transliteration and dataset analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: v1 proposes augmenting English inputs with Sanskrit stems and affixes derived from Hindi translations, explicitly making this a contribution and describing it in Section 5.1. v2 removes this procedure entirely. The principal domain-routing architecture and gating equations remain unchanged; additional implementation explanations do not establish a routing-method change.

E1.justification: The six principal target languages, eight domains and Punjabi/Malayalam human-evaluation coverage remain. Coverage narrows through removal of the English-plus-Sanskrit source-input condition evaluated in v1 Table 5. Revised sample counts and analyses of subsets of existing test data do not establish additional dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: v2 removes the Llama-based comparator from the DDST and IDDT tables and NLLB(S) from the human evaluation; the complete Sanskrit-assisted comparison also disappears. Table 1 separately reports ICL and FT LLM instead of v1's best-of-prompting-and-fine-tuning Llama-based aggregate. Both LLM approaches were already evaluated in v1, so this is not the introduction of two previously untested methods.

E3.justification: Reported IDST/IDDT test sizes change from 500 per domain/language to 10%, with an explicit 80/10/10 split. Dictionary counts change from 7926/3834/1869 to 6583/3678/1809; DDST samples increase from 100 to 500 per domain/language, and human-evaluation samples from 100 to 200. v2 adds P@1 and word-alignment-based overlap evaluation. Appendix A describes NLLB as distilled 600M instead of 630M. These are reported setting revisions, not evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 and Table 4 examine performance on overlapping versus unseen vocabulary and whether predictions merely transliterate English. Appendix B/Table 7 add dataset length and transliteration analyses, and Table 10 adds translation cases. Appendix A also reports a qualitative prompt comparison. The Sanskrit-augmentation study disappears. The routing-placement/shared-gate ablation is retained with identical results, moving from v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 5.

E5.justification: Appendix A in both versions states that results use a single run. Neither supplies uncertainty intervals, seed information or a specified significance-testing procedure. Both retain the assertion of statistically significant cross-language results without explaining a test.

E6.justification: v2 adds P@1 results, overlap/transliteration statistics and translation examples, while removing Sanskrit-assisted and zero-shot LLM entries. Some existing entries change, including BLICEr's administrative Hindi score, 54.36 to 54.21. Table 6 exchanges Base/LexGen score assignments: Punjabi R@3 changes from LexGen/Base 0.95/0.97 to 0.97/0.95, and Malayalam from 0.68/0.71 to 0.71/0.68. Most retained ChrF++ scores are identical. Revised test descriptions prevent interpreting these differences as verified same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The substantive routing and gating mathematics in Equations 1–2 is retained, with no new theorems, proofs or formal assumptions. v2 omits the standard residual layer-normalization formula while retaining its prose explanation; this does not change the mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list drop the proposed Sanskrit-based approach to coherent translation, removing one of v1's three stated contributions. The resource contribution is recast around more than 75K translation pairs, and the abstract foregrounds human evaluation already present in v1. The central domain-routing and unseen-domain/language generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning generalization beyond vocabulary overlap and transliteration, BLICEr's difficulty with unseen or multiword terms, and possible loss of encoder information when routing follows cross-attention. Sanskrit-benefit and out-of-vocabulary explanations disappear, as does the finding that NLLB(S) matches or exceeds LexGen on human recall. Limitations replace inability to exploit Sanskrit with evaluation of routing on only one MNMT backbone; the Indic-only limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents gate dimensions, approximately 480M base parameters plus 12M routing parameters, full-parameter fine-tuning, and expanded FastText/XLM-R-large details for BLICEr. It specifies five nearest-neighbor ICL examples, supplies prompt templates and adds checkpoint references. Appendix C clarifies expert evaluation without ground-truth references; Appendix B identifies the transliteration tool and provides a dataset-samples link. Most optimizer, hardware and training-time details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bafna et al. (2024), Han et al. (2023), Dou and Neubig (2021), and Madhani et al. (2022), while removing the DALI discussion and Hu et al. (2019). Positioning more explicitly emphasizes multiword limitations of induction and language-coverage limitations of LLMs. Publication updates for retained works such as NLLB do not constitute new comparison methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, related-work discussion and method/baseline explanations receive localized rewriting. Baselines become separate paragraphs, benchmark discussions gain numbered subsections, and the appendix organization changes. Author ordering, equal-contribution marking and LexGen capitalization also change. Much of the prose and the overall main-section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is retained, but the table presentation changes substantially. Table 1 separates ICL/FT rows and adds a P@1 column; zero-shot and human-evaluation tables lose comparator rows or columns. The Sanskrit table disappears, while new tables display overlap results, dataset distributions, prompts, detailed precision and translation examples. The unchanged routing-ablation table is relocated and relabeled.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful exact-match evaluation, vocabulary-generalization checks and reproducibility details. However, revised test descriptions accompany unchanged core scores, and Table 6 reverses Base/LexGen score assignments without explanation. Informative Sanskrit-assisted comparisons disappear. A new numerical inconsistency also appears: v2's administrative BLICEr entries average approximately 42.87, but Table 1 retains 42.98. These unresolved reporting issues and losses of comparative evidence prevent a reliable assessment of the net quality benefit.
